rules.statement: The fp64 oracle is the truth; bit-identity is the refactor instrument.
rules.would_be: gate: coverage.py already requires an oracle test pointer per kernel (existence only); extend it to require the test to grade against the fp64 oracle. Bit-identity as refactor-only is judgment.

rules.statement: A design is built in its best form, never correct first and fast later.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a form is the best one needs design judgment against the floors.

rules.statement: While a rule is still being discussed an agent answers what was asked and builds nothing.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a discussion is open is read from the owner's words.

rules.statement: Dense at the tensor floor, sparse well below FA toward the overhead floor; every kernel is priced against floors, never FA parity.
rules.coverage: partial: only kernels with a ROWS entry; run by hand on a GPU; does not check latency falling with sparsity, and does not stop a parity pricing.

rules.statement: Matching FA at sparse N = L while doing less work is a failure reported as an unexplained loss with a ledger.
rules.would_be: tool: the report writer refuses a sparse N = L parity cell that carries no per-resource floor-versus-measurement ledger.

rules.statement: Instructions, each pipe, shared wavefronts and bytes are each kept at what the design needs, priced on every card.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment (lab.py prints every pipe but refuses nothing).

rules.statement: Only measured binaries run.
rules.coverage: partial: the closed world is the declared targets and the gates every build runs (the toolchain, built-architecture, vendored-tree, SASS and arm gates of `//:library`); no runtime refusal of an unmeasured binary was found in the files opened.

rules.statement: No fallbacks, no dead code.
rules.coverage: partial: finds unreferenced names, templates no compiled unit instantiates and two name shapes; a fallback path or a second path doing the same job is seen only by the reviewer's obsolescence pass, whose `warn` is advisory.

rules.statement: Nothing branches the algorithm to dodge one configuration's cost.
rules.coverage: partial: only `if (kDv|DV|dv == literal)` in csrc; any other configuration-dodging branch is invisible.

rules.statement: A subsystem's interface lands first; an unbuilt part raises a named error; no parallel old path is kept.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Telling a silent fallback or a parallel old path from a legitimate second function needs reading intent; the reviewer prompt has an obsolescence pass for it.

rules.statement: A problem the kernel can solve is solved at its root, never a band-aid, shim, padding hack or for-now residue.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a change is a root fix or a band-aid is judgment.

rules.statement: A skip is an exact zero the routing activation produced, never a threshold, epsilon floor or straight-through operator.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Distinguishing an activation's exact zero from an inserted threshold needs the semantics of the code path.

rules.statement: Build the whole design, or stop and name the gap.
A new foundation lands first (contracts, derivations, primitives); the body is built bottom-up in final form, never as a prototype.
Code and docs are written for the reader a decade out.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Legibility to a future reader is judgment; the reviewer prompt has a docs-altitude pass.

rules.statement: The repository references only itself.
rules.coverage: partial: home path, the scratch-repo name, worktree and scratch-dir path patterns; other outside references (URLs, sibling checkouts by relative path) are not read.

rules.statement: Every test lives in tests/unit, tests/integration or tests/oracle, or in measure/; no per-campaign test directories.
rules.coverage: partial: checks the directories directly under tests/ only; measure/ and nested directories are not read.

rules.statement: No campaign names in the tree; names are roles.
rules.coverage: partial: a regex of work codes; a baseline of 558 findings is grandfathered (docs/internals/tools/lint.md), only new ones fail.

rules.statement: Comments are sparse: a file header and one-to-three-line declaration blocks.
rules.coverage: partial: a threshold and a block-length cap, not 'one-to-three lines' nor 'purpose and one invariant'.

rules.statement: Comments state what the code does and why, in the present tense; never a past state, stage id or comparison to what was.
rules.coverage: partial: a fixed list of history phrases and the work-code regex; a baseline of findings is grandfathered.

rules.statement: Derivations and why-not-the-other-form prose live in docs/internals/, which mirrors csrc/.
rules.coverage: partial: the mirror's shape and names, not that the prose was moved there.

rules.statement: Docs are the whole current state and reference nothing outside: no log, plan or tracker.
rules.coverage: partial: catches one named external repo path; a reference to a plan or tracker by another name is seen only by the reviewer.

rules.statement: A doc states what is; the past appears only as rationale; removals are recorded in DELETIONS.md and git only.
rules.coverage: partial: mirror pages only, and only identifiers that left the tree; 'removals recorded nowhere else' is unchecked.

rules.statement: Every mechanism states its hopper and blackwell form at design time; a one-architecture mechanism is a workaround.
No sm_86 schedule, atom, branch or plan is written to make something run there.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule refusing a __CUDA_ARCH__ comparison against an 8xx value in csrc outside kernels declared as family-neutral.

rules.statement: A mechanism's form is named per family: an atom where only the instruction differs, a schedule where the structure does.
Every kernel is compile-time specialized and takes every product or declaration constant from its plan; no kernel hard-codes one.
rules.coverage: partial: a d_v-shaped `if`, and a namespace- or class-scope integer constant given as a bare number; constants in function bodies and inside expressions are unchecked.

rules.statement: A kernel's shared memory is declared only through SmemLayout; the token __shared__ stands nowhere else.
rules.coverage: partial: the token __shared__ in the kernels' sources and the planner's headers outside common/smem_layout.cuh; a declaration spelled by a macro or an alias is not seen.

rules.statement: A SmemLayout tile's size is an expression of the build's facts, never a number: a Fixed COUNT or Share LEAST is not an integer literal.
rules.coverage: partial: a bare integer literal as the third argument of Fixed or Share; a number behind a name, a cast or parentheses, and a tile through an alias are not seen.

rules.statement: A quantity the card decides is derived at compile time; a namespace or class constant that is a bare number states why it is FIXED.
rules.coverage: partial: a text heuristic over one-line constexpr integer declarations at namespace or class scope; function-scope constants, literals inside expressions, non-integer types and a split declaration are not seen.

rules.statement: The caller passes no hardware fact; the entry selects the schedule; Python reads a hardware fact only where C++ cannot serve.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint refusing device-capability reads in fsla/ Python outside the oracle and measurement tools.

rules.statement: A primitive never selects a wider-type emulation on a target architecture; a missing operation is a declared fact, not an #if.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on #if/if constexpr architecture branches inside common/atoms that select a different-width path.

rules.statement: No path keys on a measured statistic but a side's per-level density beside the masks, which picks a layout through uniform_switch, never a result.
rules.coverage: partial: only a d_v-shaped `if`; a branch on any measured statistic is unchecked.

rules.statement: Every CTA-uniform structure branch in device code is a uniform_switch<Set>; a hand-written device switch on a geometry field is a finding.
rules.coverage: partial: a text heuristic for switches and == chains; the set's count assert, compile-time exhaustiveness, launch refusal and post-build sweep are not checked; one finding is baselined.

rules.statement: A data-dependent path whose criterion cannot be restated as a user-declared, kernel-certified bound stays out.
The library makes a prefill level-side no mask, and states its density byte 255, exactly where its declared activation cannot make exact zeros.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A level-side whose density byte is 255 is computed with every digit live and its mask is never read.
rules.coverage: partial: the reference only (an absent entry gives exactly the result of an all-ones mask); no kernel reads the density yet.

rules.statement: Every design states its cost in each regime; stages are probed at both ends; a mechanism winning one regime by losing another is a finding.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a design or measurement is overfit to one cell is judgment.

rules.statement: Every pattern of group sizes is provided; no side needs a level walked whole; performance is promised only for the built-for regime.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment: which patterns have arms is the contract's and the build checks it; whether a mechanism leans on a level walked whole is a design reading

rules.statement: A compile-time axis is a deterministic function of the declaration the selector can pick; everything else is derived or constant.
rules.coverage: partial: integer template parameters of carry __global__ kernels versus the declared key; decode and producer kernels, and the window constants, are not read.

rules.statement: Register shape and shared-memory layout are compiled from the card's facts; a call's need is a seam refusal; no runtime trip count in register-shaped loops.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment (a seam-refusal test would be a gate row if the test lane were in //:gate).

rules.statement: A descriptor is bound at the first call and checked after; the kernel refuses a ragged N, never pads.
rules.would_be: gate: put the kernel-boundary refusal tests into //:gate (today they run only in the test lane).

rules.statement: The API accepts any shape and pads; the kernel accepts only the strict shape; a lint keeps logical-width fields out of kernel entry signatures.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on kernel entry signatures naming logical-width fields. The lint the constitution names does not exist.

rules.statement: API tests prove padded runs bit-identical; kernel-boundary tests call the launch surface unpadded and assert the refusal.
rules.would_be: gate: run those tests in //:gate, or gate that each entry has a boundary-test pointer in coverage.json.

rules.statement: Decode's unit is the atom; prefill's carve owns whole rows; a kernel consumes activity bits at its own grain.
One resident CTA per SM; exposed latency is a coverage finding, never grounds to split the CTA.
rules.would_be: tool: the census reports residency per arm; assert one CTA per SM at the shipped launch.

rules.statement: A package user never registers an arm; unknown declarations are admitted by a refusal-checked derivation, never by enumeration.
rules.would_be: gate: a drift guard refusing a registration entry point in the public fsla surface (second_arm_table reads literal arm tables only).

rules.statement: Operands are the bf16 family: u8 unit-max level rows with fp32 scale, bf16 values; MMA operands bf16.
Accumulate in fp32; the output width across CTAs is the plan's (fp32 or f16), each form gated by forcing it; no precision switch by card.
The state reaches the readout through its shared-memory image stored once a window; a register readout is not built until a measurement shows it wins.
Each component has one form across densities and cards unless measurements show no single form wins; the family's error is recorded in precision.md.
Dense and sparse are plans of the one body, never a second body.
rules.coverage: partial: two __global__ names differing by an infix; a second body under a different name is unseen.

rules.statement: A ruling that changes a law is written into the standards in the stage that implements it; the milestone carries the drift guards.
A CTA owns its carve (hopper: 512 leaves, apportioned by the sides' densities), loaded and stored at entry and exit; accumulator placement changes no ownership.
The carve is decided apart from the folds' split: along a level the write side groups smaller than the level first, otherwise one walked whole.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment: the split is an output of the prefill launch function, which is not built; until it is, which level a design splits along is a design reading

rules.statement: Every asynchronous operation states its completion and issue edges per shared tenant in its ledger; a review refuses a tenant naming only the wait.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether another warp's last read stands behind the issue edge needs the barrier protocol read warp by warp.

rules.statement: A kernel's cost rises along a curve; a path change at a data-overrunnable capacity needs a stated strong reason.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Telling a plan-fixed capacity from a data-overrunnable one is judgment.

rules.statement: Every mechanism states how its cost grows with N, D, density and architecture; a cache is priced as if it does not hold.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a design block states the growth honestly is judgment.

rules.statement: Work partitions into independent units across CTAs joining by disjoint writes, reductions or atomics; a CTA waiting on another needs a strong reason.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Recognizing cross-CTA waiting in a kernel needs reading the protocol.

rules.statement: A faster form that breaks 1-3 is chosen only with the reason and numbers written down.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether the written reason is adequate is judgment.

rules.statement: q, k, v are scaled blocks in R17's forms; a routing entry is never negative; the factory refuses an entry its form does not hold.
rules.would_be: gate: put the factory refusal tests into //:gate; judgment for the form itself.

rules.statement: The op is defined on the blocks' products alone, the same for every consumer and the oracle; no level need sum to 1.
A producer folds its gain or simplex into the blocks, invisible to kernels and the oracle; a caller's levels reach the format through the factory.
A consumer needing a scale-free quantity computes it from the rows itself.
A plan field names an action, never a data property; the op's inputs carry none; the op reads no row to find what is live.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint refusing plan field names that spell a data property (dense, sparse, live count). The rule itself records the op still reads provenance (open-work rows A-c, A-e).

rules.statement: No library kernel issues a tensor step wider than 64 columns; a layout wider than a step is several 64-column steps on one A operand.
rules.coverage: partial: reads the `wgmma.mma_async` mnemonic as written in csrc/fsla source (comments excepted); a shape built by a template argument or string pieces, a step of another family and a built library's SASS are not read; HOPPER'S form only (a wgmma step's shape pins its accumulator's registers): blackwell's tcgen05 steps are not read, blackwell's widest step and where its shape is chosen being owed with its bring-up (CONSTITUTION R25, ON BLACKWELL; open-work C-n); measure/lab is exempt by design (`wgmma_width` measures wide steps).

rules.statement: A group is a layout executed by shaped steps; a step's shape is chosen once a call, from the call's densities, before any window loop.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment: whether a kernel's steps fit its layout and where it chooses the shape is a design reading; the width of a step is the gate row's

rules.statement: A group issues the number of steps its data needs, read from the packet, by a loop whose test is a warp vote.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment: no library kernel holds a grouped fold yet; whether a kernel's step count is its data's and its loop's test a vote is a design reading until the carry has a kernel for the SASS gate to read

rules.statement: The constitution is Blake's standing rulings, above every law.
rules.why: a pointer to the constitution; its rules have their own rows

rules.statement: The laws are the coordinator's dated, revisable rules; a law never contradicts the constitution.
rules.why: a definition of what this document is

rules.statement: Master is hopper only; ampere is the frozen branch; blackwell is tabulated, not built.
rules.why: restates CONSTITUTION#r8 (this line is hopper's and blackwell's), whose rows hold the rule

rules.statement: Every rule is PROCESS, [COMPILER] or [MACHINE]; a new card re-checks the latter two.
A card's rates are its rows of the hardware table, each citing its lab record.
rules.coverage: partial: a row's measured source must match the lab record it names; that a row cites one at all, and a quoted number beside a rule, are not checked.

rules.statement: Every rule of both documents has a row in docs/rules.json naming its mechanism and enforcer.
rules.coverage: partial: a row names an enforcer that resolves, not one that checks the rule; the reviewer reads the rest

rules.statement: A new rule never lands as owed; the owed list only shrinks.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: Owed to the first hopper schedule: the SASS gate's hopper model and step cover, and each kernel's budget file.
rules.would_be: gate: coverage.py already holds per-kernel owed entries for budget and phases; the hopper model itself is not a row.

rules.statement: Owed: the family's part harness, phase ledger, composer and calibrations.
rules.would_be: gate: coverage.py phases obligation (owed entries today).

rules.statement: Owed: hopper's rows of the hardware table and the price list from its labs.
rules.would_be: gate: check_hardware already refuses a built architecture with no rate row; the price list has no check.

rules.statement: Owed: every [COMPILER] rule's re-check and every [MACHINE] rule's run on sm_90a.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint that each tagged rule names a lab record for the architecture it holds on.

rules.statement: Owed: the sm_90a arms declared in the carry's arms.bzl and built.
rules.would_be: gate: check_arch_coverage reads the built architectures per tabulated arch; today it reports the unbuilt row.

rules.statement: Owed first: the family's measured timeline and the model reproducing it; composition work stops at it.
Every brief points to these standards and every review applies them line by line.
rules.coverage: partial: the review runs after the commit, is skipped mid-rebase or without the claude CLI, and refuses the next commit only on a block finding; a brief that omits the pointer is unchecked

rules.statement: Register-resident data is addressed by fragment modes only; a nest's body count is stated in the decl block and is O(fragments).
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on static_for/unroll nests bounded by a leaf or channel count; ratify (s9) records the body count.

rules.statement: An accumulator becomes the next GEMM's operand by in-place relayout and narrowing, not by store or shuffle.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a copy is the named transfer or an ad-hoc move needs reading the dataflow.

rules.statement: Every shared tile has a named layout with a derived swizzle and a round-trip test proving exactness and conflict-freedom.
Primitives (matrix load, async copy, MMA, reduction) are wrapped once in their atom under common/atoms; call sites use the wrapper.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule refusing inline asm or raw ldmatrix/cp.async/mma outside csrc/fsla/src/common/atoms.

rules.statement: Overlap needs two stages in flight; sync carries landed and drained by mbarrier, or a named barrier between roles; no implicit loop-parity state.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a protocol keeps two stages and names its parity invariant needs reading the kernel.

rules.statement: A warp is specialized only where its registers move with its role and the accumulator binds.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a role's registers move with it is a design judgment.

rules.statement: setmaxnreg is ignored in a kernel stating no register count at entry; each role's whole body stays in its own branch.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule refusing setmaxnreg in a kernel without __launch_bounds__.

rules.statement: Few warps with filled registers; warp count and budget are swept jointly; a loss there is a defect to locate, not a reason to leave.
Unroll only compile-time-bounded fragment-mode loops; dynamic loops carry #pragma unroll 1 explicitly.
rules.coverage: partial: bound judged by a naming-convention regex; accepts any numeric pragma; scoped by brace counting.

rules.statement: A static_for whose bound is a leaf count, channel count or product of them is wrong.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on static_for bounds with a leaf/channel-count name.

rules.statement: One arm per translation unit, generated from the closed-world arm list.
rules.coverage: partial: the macro refuses a malformed declaration at analysis; the decode family's list builds no per-arm unit, so only the fixture family exercises the unit generation.

rules.statement: Iteration builds are single-arch and narrowed-contract (a declared narrowed contract); every-arch full-contract builds once per stage.
rules.would_be: hook: a PreToolUse rule refusing a bazel library build without --//:archs outside a milestone.

rules.statement: Each arm has a compile budget (wall time, cicc peak RSS) read from the build's compiles.
rules.would_be: tool: ratify --census reads and a gate ratchets compile wall and cicc RSS per arm (neither is read today; the standards say so).

rules.statement: Feature selection lives where the primitive is defined, never as #if at call sites.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule refusing #if __CUDA_ARCH__ outside common/atoms.

rules.statement: Only measured binaries run: the declared targets, the built architectures, the pinned toolchain, the device stamp.
rules.coverage: partial: duplicate of CONST closed world; the declared targets and per-build gates hold it, the stamp ties a binary to its source.

rules.statement: An instruction difference is an atom, a structure difference a schedule in <kernel>/<family>/, semantics in <kernel>/.
One host call selects card and arm and refuses by name an untabulated architecture, uncarried build or unbuilt arm.
rules.would_be: gate: put the selection refusal tests into //:gate.

rules.statement: The capability rows hold only what plans, admission and atoms read; a fact nothing reads is not tabulated.
rules.coverage: partial: generated header equals the json and rates have sources; an unread row is not found.

rules.statement: ratify --census reports regs, stack, spills and residency per arm on demand; a discarded bound fails it. Compile wall, cicc RSS owed.
rules.coverage: partial: spills and registers only; compile wall, cicc RSS and nest body counts are read nowhere; the census is an on-demand report, not a gate per commit.

rules.statement: The device stamp is asserted before any gate.
rules.would_be: tool: every gate entry point asserts the stamp; only ratify reads the csrc stamp today.

rules.statement: Restates: oracle is truth, bit-identity refactor-only, no fallbacks or dead code, comments only in headers, build the whole design.
rules.why: restates CONSTITUTION rules (correctness instruments, one form per mechanism, self-documenting code, build the whole design), whose rows hold them

rules.statement: A hang or run-to-run miscount is diagnosed with the debugger or sanitizer within the first hour; the finding is recorded.
Never place a warp collective inside a short-circuit or lane-divergent predicate; hoist it and predicate its result.
rules.coverage: partial: shfl, ballot, syncwarp, all, any under &&, ||, ?:; not ldmatrix, not redux or match, not a lane-divergent if.

rules.statement: In a publish/consume pair every lane that issued the data executes the fence, and every reader fences after the broadcast.
rules.coverage: partial: a __threadfence* inside an `if (x == y)` only; the reader-side fence, ptx fence forms and other predicates are unchecked.

rules.statement: A recipe for cuda-gdb under WSL with a FIFO.
A changed protocol's brief restates the whole mechanism as pseudocode and the function is rebuilt from it, deleting the old.
A rebuild is diffed against the bug list of what it replaces before its first build.
Run a long build in the background and end the turn; no polling without a stated reason; never edit a source mid-build.
rules.coverage: partial: refuses a shell loop that sleeps or lists processes, `watch` over one and a bare sleep of 30 s or more, and lets the bounded `timeout <=600 tail --pid` through; `pgrep -f` outside a loop, an edit of a source mid-build and a launch with no background are unchecked. Fires only where the dispatcher is installed (`bazel run //:init`) and the checkout is under a root of `~/.claude/repo_hooks_roots.json`; a command is read as text, so a wait built by a variable, a script file or a quoted `bash -c` string is unseen, and a `POLL_OVERRIDE=<why>` in the command lifts it, as section 14 allows (a stated reason).

rules.statement: Compiles, disassembly, profiles, sanitizer runs, builds and installs run as graph actions, never typed in a checkout.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A launch appends a BUILD_EXIT marker; the wait is a bounded timer with early exit; the agent reads the marker first.
rules.would_be: hook: a PreToolUse rule requiring the marker on a background build command.

rules.statement: Every GPU container mounts the host's lock directory at the one lock path.
rules.coverage: partial: checked when container_check runs, not per GPU container started.

rules.statement: One gate container at a time; stop the previous run before the next.
rules.would_be: tool: the container command takes a lock and refuses a second.

rules.statement: The compile budget is machine-wide and tool-enforced: every build takes machine-wide slots through the front door.
rules.would_be: tool: a repo check that every build action runs through bazel/front_door.py; the slots are fsla-devtools' (outside this repo), so the repo enforces none today.

rules.statement: A stage has a budget of three full build-and-gate cycles; when spent and red, it stops and reports.
rules.would_be: tool: a per-stage cycle counter in the front door that refuses a fourth.

rules.statement: Re-scoping that changes what is built restarts the cycle budget; amendments that do not go in the next brief.
A development build compiles an arm subset only through a declared narrowed contract; the gate and releases enforce the full contract.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A build's jobs are the host-budget slots divided by host.nvcc_threads, under the machine-wide pool.
rules.would_be: tool: a repo check of the jobs a build is given; the sizing is fsla-devtools' (outside this repo), so the repo enforces none today.

rules.statement: A stage's gate is an iteration build, the oracle and census on its arms, and the model tests.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment: what a stage touched is the reviewer's to read; the per-build gates run regardless.

rules.statement: Every stage gate runs the fixed two-cell probe and records it; above 1.10x on either cell is red.
rules.would_be: tool: a probe target that diffs against the previous stage's record and refuses above 1.10x.

rules.statement: Every ledger table carries IPC and top stall reasons; a stage whose instructions fall while its time rises is red.
rules.would_be: tool: the ledger writer refuses a row without IPC and stalls and flags instructions-down time-up.

rules.statement: Each stage records per-arm compile wall and cicc RSS beside the previous stage's; above 1.2x on any arm is red.
rules.would_be: tool: a tool records per-arm compile wall and cicc RSS and ratchets 1.2x (none records either today; the standards say so).

rules.statement: Arm translation units never include torch headers.
rules.coverage: partial: scoped to csrc/fsla/src/<family>/ of every family the arm registry (`ARM_FAMILIES`, bazel/arms.bzl) names, the sources the family's arm units include; an arm unit's other includes are unchecked.

rules.statement: Arms are added as reviewed rows in the one arm list, TEST-tagged unless shipped.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a row is justified and correctly tagged is judgment on a diff to the declaration.

rules.statement: A gate reading profiler counters runs on a host granting them, or its row carries a written exception naming host and stand-in reading.
rules.coverage: partial: lab runs only; overlap_gate and the probe were not opened.

rules.statement: CTA-identical derivations are derived once and published behind an existing barrier or split by executor, never recomputed per warp.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Recognizing identical per-warp derivations across a kernel is semantic.

rules.statement: A kernel's SASS depends on its TU neighbors; byte-identity is a claim about a partition; per-arm TUs make bodies canonical.
Staged versus straight is decided by time, IPC and stall reasons; counts describe.
Anything the repo depends on lives in the repo or a named sibling repository, never in an ad-hoc place.
rules.coverage: partial: duplicate of CONST portability; pattern-based.

rules.statement: Briefs, transcripts, per-session scripts and campaign journals stay outside and are cited from the queue.
rules.would_be: gate: a path allow-list of tracked top-level locations.

rules.statement: Absolute paths under a home directory are a lint finding.
rules.coverage: partial: tree-wide the regex is /home/<user>/ only; /Users, /root and drives are read only under .claude/ and CLAUDE.md.

rules.statement: Committed records carry repo-relative or host-keyed locations.
rules.would_be: gate: extend the portability scan to the records' location fields.

rules.statement: A tool that could run one of two ways refuses with the fixing command; it never silently takes the other path.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment (instances exist: unit_lints fails on no verdict, sass_gate on no target).

rules.statement: A legitimate mode is keyed on an explicit declared variable and carries its exit condition on a card.
Per-file comment fraction in csrc is red above the threshold; a //: prose block outside a header is a finding.
rules.coverage: partial: a flat 15% and a 6-line block cap; 'never raises a ratio' is not a ratchet.

rules.statement: A commit bypasses the hooks only with explicit per-commit authorization; red hooks are fixed, never routed around.
rules.coverage: partial: refuses `git commit` or `git push` with `--no-verify`, `git commit -n` and `git -c core.hooksPath=...`; `git config core.hooksPath`, an environment that disables the hooks and a bypass by a script are unseen, and that an authorization is the owner's is not checked (the words after `NO_VERIFY_AUTHORIZED=` are taken). Fires only where the dispatcher is installed (`bazel run //:init`) and the checkout is under a root of `~/.claude/repo_hooks_roots.json`; a command is read as text, so one built by a variable or run from a script file is unseen.

rules.statement: The lane runs memcheck, synccheck and initcheck on each kernel's one-CTA cells when a component lands and on a schedule; never per commit.
rules.coverage: partial: runs on demand; the cadence is not enforced; each kernel has a row or an owed entry.

rules.statement: The lane reports zero hazards; a killed target is a failing gate; benign races are not tolerated.
rules.coverage: partial: racecheck is deferred for every kernel; killed-target handling was not opened.

rules.statement: Each component has a budget line in the brief before code: floors, instruction budget, and who executes it how many times.
Each component is measured in its part harness and accepted within 1.3x its binding floor and its instruction budget.
rules.coverage: partial: instruction budget only; no 1.3x binding-floor check, no regression store.

rules.statement: The composed kernel carries a phase ledger compared with the sum of its parts; the difference is reported.
rules.would_be: tool: lab.py ledger refuses a composed kernel whose phase ledger is missing (coverage.py phases only checks a pointer or an owed entry).

rules.statement: Per-component instruction counts of the shipped binary are attributed by region_ledger against tools/budgets/<kernel>.json; over budget is red.
rules.coverage: partial: run by hand over an ncu CSV; tools/budgets/ does not exist, so it has no target today (the standards say so).

rules.statement: Every kernel has its budget file, or an owed or exempt entry in tools/coverage.json saying why not.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: The kernel is composed from stub components before any is implemented; a component is never written outside its form.
A design verdict is never drawn from a build whose components have not passed their gates.
A cross-phase lever is taken only after every phase it composes passes its gate at the cell's step count.
LDL/STL or a stack frame is red: static indices only, compile-time arguments to constexpr helpers, lambdas only where inlined.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A CALL.REL.NOINC into a convergence subroutine a converged warp executes is red; collectives sit at the top level of uniform loops.
rules.coverage: partial: guarded fallbacks are counted and not red, by the 2026-09-29 ruling.

rules.statement: @P HMMA or a pair body whose non-tensor count equals its if-guarded block is red; a warp-uniform if is branched, not predicated.
rules.coverage: partial: predicated HMMA only; the pair-body instruction-count signature is not read.

rules.statement: BSSY/BSYNC per item in an unrolled all-live loop is the predicated-chain form; use a straight block when all live, a jump table when one is.
rules.would_be: tool: sass_gate counts BSSY per unrolled item (the checker's step_branches, through the gate, counts them only inside a step's loop).

rules.statement: A convergence barrier or forward conditional branch inside the innermost MMA loop is red.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A warp's copy tasks are contiguous in memory across its lanes; coalescing is checked by l1tex__t_requests per sector.
rules.would_be: tool: lab.py or overlap_gate reads l1tex__t_requests per sector and refuses above the ideal.

rules.statement: Executed instructions over the MMA count above the arm's stated ceiling make the kernel issue-bound and are red.
rules.would_be: tool: sass_gate holds a `step_density` bound a declaration states (a static count) but no arm declares one (the standards say so); declare the budget's.

rules.statement: Control a branch around collectives reads belongs in the uniform datapath; a data-dependent loop exits on a vote.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment (the unguarded-call symptom is red under s20.2).

rules.statement: A kernel parameter captured by reference is const __grid_constant__; a large body dispatches through force-inlined frames.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on kernel parameters captured by a lambda.

rules.statement: A loop bounded by a per-thread value with shuffles inside loses convergence; take its bound from lane 0 by a shuffle.
rules.would_be: gate: an ast-grep rule on a loop bound derived from threadIdx containing a collective.

rules.statement: Same grid and block, baseline on its own schedule, instructions and cycles beside time, GPU quiet, clock rows accepted.
rules.coverage: partial: the quiet-GPU condition only.

rules.statement: A change to a shared body is timed at sparse and dense at scale before it is called a win.
A design comparison quotes every family this line builds; a form that wins on one card and loses on another is flagged.
Every build runs the SASS composition, life ranges, oracle, phase ledger, region ledger, tensor utilization, A/B, census, composer, calibrations and timeline, as one diffed report.
rules.would_be: tool: one measure target emitting the diffed report on every build.

rules.statement: A component's theory is written before the build; a miss is explained by an isolating measurement before anything is reverted.
A probe that can report a stale artifact is a suite defect fixed before its numbers are used.
Every number computed by hand in a debug session becomes a permanent step of the gate the same day.
A kernel's measured timeline and the model reproducing it are the first thing built for a family; composition work stops at it.
Every machine-dependent value is declared in tools/dev_config.py and read through that loader; a replaced variable is deleted, never a fallback.
rules.coverage: partial: .py, .sh and hook files; two machine-path patterns; a kept fallback is unchecked.

rules.statement: tools/dev.py targets alone set up and check a host; a new machine value lands with schema key, init detection and check row.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint that each dev_config SCHEMA key has a check row in dev.py (cmd_check exists, forces nothing).

rules.statement: The commit gate refuses a tree whose devbox image is not the one tools/devbox_image.json names, or a changed name without a passing record.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A broken or slow build, dev loop or measurement system is fixed before the next kernel optimization.
A step is one block with no data-dependent branch; sparsity is a shorter list, never a skip; the list is built by lanes at once.
rules.coverage: partial: functions issuing ops::*mma* only (wgmma atoms not read); forbids vote, warp sync, barrier, while, data if, fence, unroll 1 in a burst function; two-loops and lane-built lists are unchecked.

rules.statement: A hopper design states its decide and burst tiers in its steady-state timeline.
A dependence is hidden only by what sits between its ends in the SASS, never by the source.
Order by data dependency, never by hope; no fence or clock trick. Independent loads may be issued together under ops::launch_known.
rules.coverage: partial: a fence inside a burst function only; a clock trick or fence elsewhere is unchecked; the exception's one use rests on the decode step's record (docs/internals/decode/decode.md#atom-loads), and the library's SASS gate counts a load issued behind another load's wait in every kernel (the checker's load_behind_load, 0 allowed).

rules.statement: Space the loads first and push stores down; about eight instructions between a matrix load and its consumer.
rules.would_be: tool: the sass gate's exposed-latency reading (owed to the family model).

rules.statement: A component states its live-register cost; the gate prints the arm's distance to the next threshold.
rules.would_be: tool: sass_gate prints regs only; add the distance to the next allocation threshold.

rules.statement: Nothing below ptxas is patched unless the coverage reading shows the order right and only the bits wrong.
A model simulates every calibration row's loop and prints it beside the measurement; a floor is ratcheted only while it reproduces the rows.
rules.would_be: tool: a model tool refuses to ratchet a floor on a loop whose rows it does not reproduce.

rules.statement: A model is trusted only after two forms of the same loop are measured and both reproduced.
A row is named by its access pattern, which is the kernel's; every row's header states its pattern.
rules.would_be: tool: lab.py refuses an experiment header with no pattern marker, as it does for TIMELINE:.

rules.statement: A tool comparing a measurement to an ideal states where the ideal's count comes from.
A stall census is read per line; the isolating measurement for a model miss is the per-line census of two forms.
A large body is one copy with its variant a runtime value chosen by a register select, never an index.
rules.coverage: partial: the symptoms (spill, outlined call) only; single-copy form is not checked.

rules.statement: A probe's placement is read off its SASS; a row whose placement differs from the kernel's measures a different thing.
A stub prices only its own access pattern; read what it writes before a part switch's trivial form is called a win.
tools/kernels.py is the kernel list; the build, ratify and every gate read it; no tool keeps a second list.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint refusing a __global__ scan in tools/ outside kernels.py.

rules.statement: A gate takes its targets from the list and fails when it finds none; a narrowing is a measurement, never a gate.
rules.coverage: partial: sass_gate and coverage.py; overlap_gate, life_ranges and region_ledger were not shown to fail on no target.

rules.statement: tools/coverage.json declares per kernel the oracle, sanitizer, budget, phases and overlap obligation; an undeclared kernel or dead pointer fails.
rules.coverage: partial: owed entries are accepted as the reviewed backlog, and pointers are checked for existence, not for meeting the obligation.

rules.statement: Source gates run in the commit gate; binary gates after every build.
The analyzer is pinned to a release that parses every unit, and a parse error fails the gate.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: A device file may mark a region //: @barrier-free; a CTA or grid barrier inside one fails, as does an unclosed region.
rules.coverage: partial: __syncthreads, bar.sync, cluster and grid sync by regex; other barrier spellings are unchecked.

rules.statement: A hardware or compiler claim is a rule only when a lab experiment measured it, and the rule names the experiment, record and architectures.
rules.would_be: gate: a lint that every [MACHINE]/[COMPILER] rule names a measure/lab/results record that exists.

rules.statement: An experiment's number counts only after its SASS gate: declared instructions present, no local memory, no undeclared convergence call.
rules.coverage: full

rules.statement: An experiment's header states its TIMELINE before the kernel is written, and every kernel is held to the loop hazards the driver reads.
rules.coverage: partial: experiments outside the _PRE_TIMELINE debt list only.

rules.statement: A lesson an agent learns is a row of LEARNINGS.md naming the hook, lint or tool check that refuses its repeat.
rules.coverage: partial: the named path::text must exist; that the named check refuses the lesson is not checked.

rules.statement: A warp collective's enclosing control flow derives from kernel arguments, the block index or constants.
rules.coverage: partial: duplicate of s20.2; the symptom (a call) not the source form.

rules.statement: Issue a past-the-end reduction step as an exact zero, never a branch around the add; a dead lane adds at its CTA's own row.
A step's body is one basic block: no conditional load, no lane-predicated atomic, no runtime switch over registers.
rules.coverage: partial: duplicate of s27.1.

rules.statement: Every streaming lab and gate prices the floor on read plus write bytes at a flat stream's rate measured in the same run.
rules.would_be: tool: overlap_gate's DRAM floor uses profiler bytes; whether it covers writes was not verified.

rules.statement: No branch between a stage's prefetch and its MMAs or around its adds; a padded entry is made safe, never skipped.
rules.coverage: partial: branches in the innermost MMA loop of a built cubin; 'a padded entry is made safe' is unchecked.

rules.statement: Never an if around a load, store or atomic, and never a predicated memory operation in a step.
rules.coverage: partial: functions issuing MMAs; the SASS side (the resulting branch) is s27.1.

rules.statement: Register-resident state is indexed only at compile time; never a runtime switch to select registers.
rules.coverage: partial: the symptoms; the source form is unchecked.

rules.statement: A register ring of depth D is unrolled by D, never rotated by copies in a rolled loop.
rules.would_be: tool: sass_gate reports register moves per MMA and reds the copy-rotation signature; STATS carries no such count (the standards no longer claim it).

rules.statement: The outer dynamic loop is #pragma unroll 1 and its body the unrolled stages; a remainder is padded or peeled.
rules.coverage: partial: the outer pragma only; unrolled stages and padding are unchecked.

rules.statement: Read the interleave in the SASS, never the source; a data dependency is the only lever that places an MMA.
A kernel is priced at the largest of its floors and its budget names the overlap that makes it so.
rules.coverage: partial: rows only for kernels with a perf cell; several kernels are owed an overlap row.

rules.statement: A phase between barriers that idles the binding stream is a design defect: overlap it or prove none exists.
rules.coverage: partial: sees the aggregate ratio, not which phase idles.

rules.statement: A line is never lowered to admit a serial phase: a time above the line is red and the design changes.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Editing LINE or a floor in a diff is visible to a reader; no check pins the constant.

rules.statement: A phase whose warps stall on one dependent chain interleaves independent work into it.
rules.would_be: tool: the phase ledger and stall census (s32.2).

rules.statement: Before code, a budget by opcode class per MMA, derived from the design at the declared regime; in the lab Bench::budget.
rules.coverage: partial: labs only; production budget files do not exist (tools/budgets/ absent), coverage accepts owed.

rules.statement: Every value is computed at the outermost level its inputs allow, within the register line.
The base is computed once at its level; each access is an immediate or one add; a swizzle is folded into the base.
A pad token's base is the lane's dummy row, chosen once a token a step; never a select per element.
The facts pass emits only the data's own facts and nothing of a card's; on hopper no pass hands the carry a list or operand.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment; the standards mark this item ruled and not built (open-work A-e).

rules.statement: An fp32-to-integer conversion is one FFMA adding 1.5 x 2^23; the conversion unit is never in a step unless a lab declares it.
rules.coverage: partial: innermost MMA loops only.

rules.statement: A step's operands are staged ahead by the family's copy; a reduction to global memory is a drain outside the steps.
rules.coverage: partial: innermost MMA loops; the staged copy forms are allowed.

rules.statement: Every recorded variant checks outputs against a host reference or states why not; every MMA kernel has a budget or exemption.
rules.coverage: partial: six experiments in _PRE_29 are exempt from the missing-check part.

rules.statement: Hold constants in registers, branch on loaded data by a vote, bottom-test data loops, prefetch into a pad, no loop in a divergent region.
rules.would_be: gate: lab.py LOOP_CONVERGENCE covers loops of experiments; production kernels need the same check in sass_gate.

rules.statement: A free-running CTA is timed by its span (WarpSpan) against the free floor, not the mean warp's cycles.
Each line item is its trips times the SASS price of its primitives from the architecture's price list; an unpriced primitive is compiled alone first.
Trips are counted per cell from the mirror, a lane-divergent loop at its longest lane; the fixed part itemized by phase.
A miss is attributed to its phase; a restated budget corrects the price list in the same commit; undeclared convergence regions in loops are refused.
rules.coverage: partial: the convergence refusal only; the price-list correction in the same commit is unchecked.

rules.statement: lab.py run prints every kernel's standard counters; count times rate bounds perfect overlap, the timeline predicts; a kernel over 1.3x its floor names its stall.
rules.coverage: partial: prints on every run and refuses nothing; the 1.3x rule is unchecked.

rules.statement: Each line item cites the cheapest known form from budgets.md#forms or says why it departs.
A wait on a commit group follows the work that does not depend on it; a wait straight after its issue is declared.
rules.coverage: partial: the checker's `wait_after_issue` rule, which the lab's check calls: a tensor wait that leaves no group in flight, its steps in straight-line code before it; a wait whose steps sit across a branch, and a wait leaving a group in flight, are not counted; the work that could precede it is advisory (lab waits).

rules.statement: Every shared buffer has an access table before code: each instruction by lanes, addresses and banks, and the shapes it is conflict-free for.
A placement constraint enters a producer's format only after the composed consumer is timed with and without it.
A pad is a free residue's row for a gather or a dummy row aligned to that residue, never a spare word.
Each budget has a wavefronts line; lab.py gates ncu's measured count against it and prints bank conflicts.
rules.coverage: partial: labs with a budget (over_budget); a lab record's profile dumps, any experiment (profile_failures: BANK_CONFLICT).

rules.statement: The producer runs tools/bank_model.py on what it emits and reports wavefronts by part.
rules.would_be: tool: the producer's test or lab inputs refuse to run without the bank-model report.

rules.statement: Conflicts are priced for dense, sparse and the W = 1024 lists.
A store whose places the data picks stands only where the owner accepts it and its page states its access table.
A warp collective is never an operand of &&, || or ?:, nor under a lane-dependent branch.
rules.coverage: partial: duplicate of s12.1; lab check covers `?` in experiment sources only.

rules.statement: The first run of new or changed device code is under timeout -s KILL with bounded waits; a hang is killed, never waited on.
rules.would_be: hook: a PreToolUse rule refusing a repo GPU entry point not wrapped in timeout -s KILL (lab.py execute has its own timeout).

rules.statement: Before components are written, the design states one warp's steady-state timeline: phases, streams, load-to-use distances, live registers.
rules.coverage: partial: experiments only; production kernels are unchecked.

rules.statement: Each phase is predicted by the timeline model and the prediction budgeted; a phase over 1.3x or unpredicted is red; a miss stops work.
rules.would_be: tool: a family phase ledger reading phase_cycles from the budget; no such ledger or file exists (the standards say so).

rules.statement: The budget's registers line states each component's peak live registers; a component past its line or without one is red.
rules.coverage: partial: run by hand; no budget file exists for it to read; not in the build or the gate (the standards say so).

rules.statement: sass_gate simulates every innermost MMA loop and reds one whose cover is under 1/1.15; a kernel under it is a named debt.
rules.would_be: tool: sass_gate with the family machine model; it runs no cover until the model exists (the standards and its page say so).

rules.statement: A floor, budget line or gate row naming a function, loop or cell the tree no longer has fails.
rules.coverage: partial: kernel and coverage pointers; budget lines and floors naming vanished functions were not shown to fail.

rules.statement: Read the common headers before writing a helper; a kernel-local copy of a common primitive is a defect, an unused one dead code.
rules.why_not_mechanical: judgment (unused instantiations and vulture catch only unreferenced names).

rules.statement: Two builds are compared only in one interleaved clock-locked session or by ncu cycles of one launch each.
Reordering work around a barrier cannot shorten warps that all do the same work; price it on the critical path first.
Stage a value in shared memory only if other warps read it, it needs rearranging, buffering beyond registers, or the MMA reads it there.
rules.why_not_mechanical: Whether a staged value has one of the four reasons needs the dataflow read; the lab STORE_RELOAD check sees only an immediate reload.

rules.statement: Contiguous rows an MMA reads from global memory are staged by the family's copy (TMA on hopper), never loaded to registers direct.
rules.would_be: gate: sass_gate step_global covers loads inside MMA loops only; extend to any LDG feeding an MMA operand.

rules.statement: Scattered rows, each its own request, are loaded by warps and stored; a copy engine serializes them.
Staging condition 1: other warps read it.
rules.why: one of the four conditions of the staging rule; the rule's rows are KERNEL_STANDARDS#s33:*

rules.statement: Staging condition 2: it must be rearranged on the way.
rules.why: one of the four conditions of the staging rule; the rule's rows are KERNEL_STANDARDS#s33:*

rules.statement: Staging condition 3: it must be buffered beyond the warp's registers.
rules.why: one of the four conditions of the staging rule; the rule's rows are KERNEL_STANDARDS#s33:*

rules.statement: Staging condition 4: the MMA reads it from shared memory.
rules.why: one of the four conditions of the staging rule; the rule's rows are KERNEL_STANDARDS#s33:*

store_unfenced.guidance: Fence the shared stores (`publish_fence()`, atoms/barrier.md#publish-fence) before the arrival that hands them to a step's warp; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s12, LEARNINGS.md#store-unfenced (pool_fill's four-producer variant failed by a different count each run).

stack_memory.guidance: Index register arrays only at compile time (`static_for`, unrolled), pass compile-time arguments to constexpr helpers and capture parameters `const __grid_constant__`; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s20, a spill's cost in docs/lab/state_image.md (16 held descriptors spill to the stack).

convergence_call.guidance: Put a collective's control flow on kernel arguments, the block index or constants, and a role's index through `uniform_warp` (atoms/warp.md#uniform-warp); a large body dispatches through `uniform_switch`; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s20, cost in docs/lab/collective_branch.md.

profiler_verdicts.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: read the verdict with its counts beside time on a quiet GPU (KERNEL_STANDARDS#s21 and #s16-addendum-4).

wait_injected.guidance: Read a step's accumulators only after its own wait: the toolkit injects a `wgmma.wait_group` where code reads registers a step defines; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized.

mma_serialized.guidance: Hold the registers a role's steps need, write a step's operand registers before its commit group, put no step under a branch the toolkit cannot prove uniform and touch no accumulator inside its stage; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized, docs/lab/carry_window.md.

clock_uniform.guidance: Make a lap that must be a thread's count its own: add a zero the toolkit cannot know is one, from the thread's index, to the reading (`cycles()`, atoms/clock.md); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#lap-in-uniform.

step_branches.guidance: A step is one basic block: no branch between its prefetch and its MMAs, a padded entry made safe not skipped, sparsity a shorter list (`uniform_switch` for a role's dispatch, atoms/warp.md#uniform-warp); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s27.1 and #s24, evidence docs/lab/collective_branch.md.

step_rolled.guidance: Write steps a straight block, or one that may be absent under a forward branch behind its own fence; for a run-time count use the plain vote loop that holds the wait (`ops::once` hides the trip, atoms/warp.md#once); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s27, evidence docs/lab/step_rolled.md (a step in a rolled loop of a run-time count 37.6 cycles a step against 23.2 straight, 1.62 times, a fence a step free) and LEARNINGS.md#step-rolled.

step_predicated.guidance: Never guard a step with an `if` that the toolkit turns into a predicate: issue an absent step as an exact zero (KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26.3.q) or behind its own branch and fence (LEARNINGS.md#step-rolled); nothing else of fsla's beyond the generic fix.

step_serialized.guidance: Keep the steps' commit groups apart: wait for the group you need (`wg_wait<N>`, KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.16) and not after every step, so the next step issues while the one before runs; a wait after every step on purpose (a reduction that needs each result) is declared with its reason (STEP_SERIALIZED); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized.

accumulator_moved.guidance: Touch a step's accumulator registers only after its own wait and never between its steps: no copy or update (`d[0] += f`) of them inside the chain, the update goes after the last wait; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized.

wait_all_with_work.guidance: Wait for fewer groups (`wg_wait<N>` with N above 0) when work that does not read the newest group follows (loads, stores, atomics, copies, barriers, arrivals): the wait for all holds that work behind the steps; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.16, LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized.

step_gap.guidance: Fill the run between two steps with work that does not read their accumulators (`wg_wait` after it, KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.16); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s28, the chain's cost in docs/lab/step_queue.md.

step_work.guidance: Budget a step's instructions by class before code (the experiment's `Bench::budget`); every added step issue is priced against its line; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.1 and #s29.14, price list in docs/internals/tools/budgets.md; declare the bound as STEP_WORK.

step_density.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: read the experiment's `Bench::budget` instruction line (KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.1) and move work out of the steps' region before adding more steps.

step_conversion.guidance: No conversion-unit instruction in a step: an fp32-to-integer conversion is one FFMA adding 1.5 x 2^23, exp and root only outside the steps (`exp2_approx`, `sqrt_approx`, atoms/math.md); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.6; declare STEP_XU where a form keeps one.

step_global.guidance: A step's operands are staged ahead by the family's copy (`stage_tile`, `stage_run`, atoms/copy.md; TMA on hopper) and a reduction to global memory is a drain outside the steps; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.7 and #s33; declare STEP_GLOBAL where a form keeps one.

loop_convergence.guidance: Bound a loop with collectives inside by a warp-uniform value (`uniform_warp`, a vote or lane 0's shuffle) so ptxas keeps convergence; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s20-addendum-2 and #s29.9, evidence docs/lab/collective_branch.md.

wait_after_issue.guidance: Put the work that does not read a group's accumulators between its issue and its wait, `lab waits` lists the candidates; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.16.

shared_wavefronts_excess.guidance: Hold each budget's wavefronts line: `tools/bank_model.py` prices a layout before code, `lab.py` gates ncu's count against it; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s30, a conflict-free layout is a line a bank (docs/lab/smem_rates.md).

step_port.guidance: Price the port before code: a step's operands plus the region's shared loads and stores, atoms/memory.md for the shared accesses; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s30 and #s29.14, rates in docs/lab/smem_rates.md; declare the bound as STEP_PORT.

loop_held.guidance: A value formed before a loop and used after it, or by every trip, is held in a register across the whole loop, and spilled where registers are scarce. Form it inside the loop from an opaque index (`ops::opaque`, atoms/warp.md#opaque) or after the loop; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s32; the decode step's fold takes its thread index through it for this reason (docs/internals/decode/decode_fold.md).

load_behind_load.guidance: Issue every load of a trip before the first use of any of their values. Where the assembler moves an independent load behind another load's wait, put the group under `ops::launch_known` (atoms/warp.md#launch-known), the one exception to KERNEL_STANDARDS#s23-addendum item 2; the record is the decode step's (docs/internals/decode/decode.md#atom-loads: 1.60 ms against 0.77).

load_in_trip.guidance: Issue the load a stage ahead of its use with the ring at fixed registers (KERNEL_STANDARDS#s32, static_for.cuh unrolls it, never rotate by copies in a rolled loop #s27.4); evidence docs/lab/fold_stream.md, LEARNINGS.md#load-in-trip.

store_reload.guidance: Keep a value no other warp reads in a register (a count through shared memory at every leaf cost a producer its trips); KERNEL_STANDARDS#s33, LEARNINGS.md#store-reload.

build_info.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: the toolkit's per-function summary lines are accepted by default; LEARNINGS.md#notices-read.

function_size.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: a function's instructions are a figure until a declaration bounds them; state the bound the kernel's budget names (KERNEL_STANDARDS#s29.1) beside its arms.

local_memory_used.guidance: Index register arrays only at compile time (`static_for`, unrolled) so no array takes a stack frame; the toolkit's own warning names the frame's size; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s20, LEARNINGS.md#notices-read.

register_spill.guidance: Lower the live state (a smaller tile, fewer accumulators in flight) or state the register count at entry (`__launch_bounds__`); a spill is local-memory traffic beside the work the kernel states; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s20, LEARNINGS.md#notices-read.

setmaxnreg_ignored.guidance: State the register count at entry (`__launch_bounds__(threads, blocks)`) and put each role's whole body inside its own branch, so the register trade happens; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#setmaxnreg-ignored.

unreachable_loop.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: a loop the front end proved unreachable measures nothing, so remove it or fix the condition; LEARNINGS.md#notices-read.

unused_variable.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: an unused name emits no instruction and is accepted by default; LEARNINGS.md#notices-read.

variable_unset.guidance: Initialize the variable on every path that reaches the read; a lambda is instantiated only in the roles that set what it captures; KERNEL_STANDARDS#s26, LEARNINGS.md#lambda-unset.

wgmma_arrive_injected.guidance: Nothing beyond the generic fix: write the fence yourself where the registers settle if the cycles matter; LEARNINGS.md#steps-serialized.
